sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: In 2010, A History of the World in 100 Objects, hosted by Neil McGregor,
sentences.zh: 2010年，由尼尔·麦格雷戈主持的《大英博物馆世界简史》

sentences.en: premiered on BBC Radio 4 to great acclaim.
sentences.zh: 在英国广播公司第四台首播，赢得了极高的赞誉。

sentences.en: It was a groundbreaking series that told a complex and interconnected history of the world
sentences.zh: 这是一个具有开创性的系列节目，它讲述了一个复杂且相互交织的世界历史，

sentences.en: through 100 objects housed in the British Museum collection.
sentences.zh: 通过大英博物馆馆藏中的100件物品来呈现。

sentences.en: For 2026, BBC Studios decided they wanted to revamp and reimagine that ambitious series,
sentences.zh: 到了2026年，BBC工作室决定对这个宏大的系列进行革新和重新构想，

sentences.en: this time focusing on the history of the United States,
sentences.zh: 这一次将聚焦于美国的历史，

sentences.en: coinciding with the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence.
sentences.zh: 恰逢《独立宣言》签署250周年之际。

sentences.en: To the great credit of the BBC, they thought that maybe British broadcasters
sentences.zh: 值得BBC高度赞赏的是，他们认为英国广播员

sentences.en: weren't the best equipped to take on the curation of 100 objects that told the history of the United States,
sentences.zh: 或许并不是最适合负责策划100件讲述美国历史的物品的人选，

sentences.en: so that's when they reached out to me, lifelong American, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 所以他们联系了我——一个地道的美国人，罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: With our 100 Objects series, we knew we wanted to get out of the museum
sentences.zh: 在我们的《100件物品》系列中，我们知道我们要走出了博物馆，

sentences.en: and focus on objects that were overlooked, thrown away, mass-produced, and misunderstood.
sentences.zh: 把焦点放在那些被忽视、被丢弃、被大量生产且被误解的物品上。

sentences.en: Not priceless museum pieces, but the everyday things that provide a portal into stories
sentences.zh: 不是那些无价的博物馆展品，而是那些日常之物，它们开启了一扇通往故事的门户，

sentences.en: about what America means to itself and to the world at large.
sentences.zh: 讲述了美国对自身以及对整个世界意味着什么。

sentences.en: But from the beginning, I knew I needed sage advice to do the job right.
sentences.zh: 但从一开始，我就知道要想把这份工作做好，我需要明智的建议。

sentences.en: And so I sought the counsel of the original 100 Objects host, Neil McGregor.
sentences.zh: 因此，我寻求了最初的《100件物品》主持人尼尔·麦格雷戈的指导。

sentences.en: Here's our conversation.
sentences.zh: 以下是我们的对话。

sentences.en: What I was hoping you could do, to begin with, is take me back to January 2010.
sentences.zh: 首先，我希望你能做的是，带我回到2010年1月。

sentences.en: A history of the world in 100 objects is launching.
sentences.zh: 《大英博物馆世界简史》即将推出。

sentences.en: It starts with a mummy that you saw as a boy.
sentences.zh: 它是从你小时候见过的一具木乃伊开始的。

sentences.en: Were you aware of the phenomenon that this was going to be when you started?
sentences.zh: 当你开始的时候，你意识到这将成为一种轰动效应吗？

sentences.en: No, absolutely not.
sentences.zh: 不，完全没有。

sentences.en: Absolutely not.
sentences.zh: 完全没有。

sentences.en: I was intimidated.
sentences.zh: 我感到很惶恐。

sentences.en: We were all intimidated by the fact that the BBC had committed to a series of 100 programmes.
sentences.zh: 我们都对BBC承诺制作100期节目这一决定感到惶恐。

sentences.en: We had no idea how it was going to be received at all.
sentences.zh: 我们完全不知道它会受到怎样的反响。

sentences.en: And in a strange way, the project began really almost as an internal project in the British Museum.
sentences.zh: 说也奇怪，这个项目最初几乎只是大英博物馆内部的一个项目。

sentences.en: What's interested me, having come from the National Gallery, a paintings collection, to a museum,
sentences.zh: 让我感兴趣的是，我从国家美术馆——一个收藏绘画作品的地方，来到了一个博物馆，

sentences.en: the ambition of which was to show really the history of humanity through things.
sentences.zh: 它的宏愿实际上是通过实物来展示人类的历史。

sentences.en: So not an art museum, but to try to explore what it meant to put objects from all over the world into one building.
sentences.zh: 所以它不是一个艺术博物馆，而是试图去探索将来自世界各地的物品放在同一栋建筑里意味着什么。

sentences.en: So it really began as a way of exploring what happens when you think of a museum as a place where different objects are exploring the same kind of human experience.
sentences.zh: 因此，它最初只是一种方式，用来探索当你把博物馆视为一个让不同物品探讨同一种人类经验的场所时，会发生什么。

sentences.en: And of all the things in the building, how did you choose the 100?
sentences.zh: 在馆内的所有物品中，你是如何选出这100件的？

sentences.en: Well, this was the greatest fun.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是最有趣的部分。

sentences.en: The British Museum is created in the middle of the 18th century, really at that moment of the Enlightenment,
sentences.zh: 大英博物馆创建于18世纪中叶，正值启蒙运动时期，

sentences.en: when people begin to have a totally different notion of what humanity means.
sentences.zh: 当时人们开始对人类的含义产生完全不同的观念。

sentences.en: It's the physical expression of that Enlightenment notion that there is one humanity.
sentences.zh: 它是启蒙运动中“人类是一个整体”这一理念的物质表达。

sentences.en: So what we decided to do was to try to organise the 100 objects.
sentences.zh: 所以我们决定尝试把这100件物品组织起来。

sentences.en: Well, the BBC decided that there would be five programmes a week, and there needed to be a theme for each week.
sentences.zh: BBC决定每周播出一档节目，共五期，并且每周需要有一个主题。

sentences.en: And we wanted to go effectively from the beginning, the earliest hand tools made by anything that can roughly be called human, right up to today.
sentences.zh: 我们希望实际上从开端讲起，从任何勉强可以被称为人类的生物制造的最早的手工工具，一直讲到今天。

sentences.en: So that gave us the format.
sentences.zh: 这就是节目的形式。

sentences.en: And that in each week, we would go round the world.
sentences.zh: 而且在每周的节目中，我们要走遍全世界。

sentences.en: So you would take, let's say, 1000 BCE, and look at a theme, let's say, power.
sentences.zh: 比如，你可以设定在公元前1000年，然后研究一个主题，比如权力。

sentences.en: I mean, how do different societies represent power at 1000 BCE?
sentences.zh: 我是说，在公元前1000年，不同的社会是如何表现权力的？

sentences.en: But what it meant internally was that for every week, I would sit down with a curator from the Chinese collection, the Indian collection, the Egyptian collection,
sentences.zh: 但从内部来看，这意味着每周我都要和来自中国馆、印度馆、埃及馆的馆长坐在一起，

sentences.en: the Americas collection.
sentences.zh: 还有美洲馆的馆长。

sentences.en: And we would have to think of what objects might speak to each other.
sentences.zh: 我们必须思考什么样的物品能够彼此呼应。

sentences.en: Of course, for academics in particular discipline, this is a totally new way of thinking.
sentences.zh: 当然，对于特定学科的学者来说，这是一种全新的思考方式。

sentences.en: There was no connection between ancient Egypt and ancient China.
sentences.zh: 古代埃及和古代中国之间并没有什么联系。

sentences.en: So no Egyptologist was likely to have asked what in my collection might relate to something that's happening at the same time in China, because there's no connection.
sentences.zh: 因此，埃及学家不太可能会去想，我收藏的什么东西能与同一时期在中国发生的事情产生关联，因为它们之间没有联系。

sentences.en: It's an anthropological question asked to people who are historical scholars.
sentences.zh: 这是一个向历史学者提出的人类学问题。

sentences.en: And they found that completely thrilling,
sentences.zh: 而他们发现这令人感到无比兴奋，

sentences.en: because it's allowed them all really to look at familiar objects and ask a totally new kind of question and suggest the commonalities of human behavior.
sentences.zh: 因为这让他们所有人都能真正审视熟悉的物品，提出一种全新的问题，并揭示人类行为的共同点。

sentences.en: Wherever we are, we all behave roughly, equally badly, equally well, and surprisingly, more or less in the same way.
sentences.zh: 无论我们身处何地，我们的大致表现其实都一样：同样糟糕，同样优秀，而且令人惊奇的是，表现方式也大同小异。

sentences.en: Were there heated arguments?
sentences.zh: 当时有激烈的争论吗？

sentences.en: Was there table pounding when people were deciding which artifacts to select?
sentences.zh: 大家在决定挑选哪些文物时，有没有拍桌子争论？

sentences.en: Curators don't normally pound the table.
sentences.zh: 策展人平时是不会拍桌子的。

sentences.en: There was a certain amount of shrill advocacy for my particular piece, and a certain amount of sulking that others didn't make it.
sentences.zh: 对于我心仪的那件藏品，大家有过一番激烈的力争，而对于落选的藏品，也有过一些生闷气的情况。

sentences.en: But it was normally extremely good timid, and because it was a new kind of conversation for all of them, very, very exciting.
sentences.zh: 但大家的交流通常都非常温和，而且由于对他们所有人来说这都是一种新型的对话，因此非常非常令人兴奋。

sentences.en: And because what we were looking at was not the history of the world, but our history, a very peculiar one.
sentences.zh: 而且因为我们所审视的并非世界历史，而是我们的历史，一段非常独特的历史。

sentences.en: And one of the histories we wanted to tell, almost unspoken through it, because every object came from the museum,
sentences.zh: 我们想要讲述的历史之一，虽然几乎未曾明说，但由于每件藏品都来自博物馆，

sentences.en: was how did it happen that every one of these objects ultimately wound up in London?
sentences.zh: 那就是：所有这些藏品最终究竟是如何汇聚到伦敦的？

sentences.en: Was there a sense that you had to present a variety of objects?
sentences.zh: 大家是否觉得必须呈现各种各样的文物？

sentences.en: Because you could certainly do a history of the world in a hundred coins.
sentences.zh: 因为你完全可以用一百枚硬币来讲述世界史。

sentences.en: The joy of a collection at the British Museum is that you have so many different media
sentences.zh: 大英博物馆藏品的奇妙之处在于，你拥有如此丰富的不同载体，

sentences.en: in which humans articulate what matters to them, which is what all these things are about.
sentences.zh: 人类用它们来表达对他们而言重要的事情，而这正是所有这些事物的意义所在。

sentences.en: But the main purpose of doing history through objects was we wanted to allow people who don't have a voice to be heard.
sentences.zh: 但通过文物来讲述历史的主要目的，是我们希望让那些没有发声权的人被听到。

sentences.en: History is, on the whole, used to mean, of course, just written history.
sentences.zh: 当然，历史总体上通常指的是文字记载的历史。

sentences.en: That limits you immediately to that small bit of humanity that wrote, and it also limits you normally to the people that were in control,
sentences.zh: 这就直接把你的视野限制在了那一小部分进行书写的全人类身上，同时也通常把你局限在了那些掌握权力的人身上，

sentences.en: because they were the ones that wrote the history, and they made sure it survived.
sentences.zh: 因为正是他们书写了历史，并且确保了这些历史得以流传。

sentences.en: So part of our project was to have a history told by the people that had never been able to tell their story through the things they made.
sentences.zh: 所以我们项目的一部分，就是让那些从未能通过自己制造的物品来讲述自身故事的人来讲述历史。

sentences.en: And that, I think, is really important.
sentences.zh: 而我认为，这真的非常重要。

sentences.en: How do you give a voice to the voiceless of the past?
sentences.zh: 你该如何赋予过去那些失语的人以声音？

sentences.en: And particularly when you're talking about indigenous histories,
sentences.zh: 尤其是当你谈论原住民历史的时候，

sentences.en: then the objects become of huge importance as carrying the stories that weren't written and may not have survived in song or myth.
sentences.zh: 然后，这些物品变得极其重要，因为它们承载着那些没有被文字记录、可能也没有在歌谣或神话中流传下来的故事。

sentences.en: So around the same time, in 2010, I launched my show called 99% Invisible, and it's about architecture and design.
sentences.zh: 所以在差不多同一时期，即2010年，我推出了我的节目《99%隐形》，它讲的是建筑和设计。

sentences.en: And there was a certain kind of perversity to doing a radio show about architecture and design, because there's hugely visual things.
sentences.zh: 而且做一档关于建筑和设计的广播节目带有一种某种程度的悖论，因为它们是极具视觉性的事物。

sentences.en: And you made the same choice to do a radio series on these things that most people take in with their eyes.
sentences.zh: 而你也做出了同样的选择，为这些大多数人通过眼睛来感受的事物制作一个广播系列节目。

sentences.en: Why did you do that?
sentences.zh: 你为什么那么做？

sentences.en: What did you get out of that?
sentences.zh: 你从中得到了什么？

sentences.en: Well, at one level, it is totally counterintuitive, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 嗯，从某种层面来看，这完全是反直觉的，对吧？

sentences.en: That we're talking about things, the materiality of things, how they're made, the skill with which they're made, and yet you can't see it.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是事物，事物的物质性、它们的制造方式、制造它们的精湛技艺，然而你却看不见它。

sentences.en: This is where I think the BBC radio, they know how to do this.
sentences.zh: 这就是我认为BBC广播厉害的地方，他们懂得怎么做这个。

sentences.en: But it's not just that.
sentences.zh: 但不仅如此。

sentences.en: BBC has, I think, understood very profoundly and built on the fact that if you can only hear something, then you have to imagine what it is.
sentences.zh: 我认为BBC深刻地理解并建立在这样一种基础上：如果你只能听到某种东西，那么你就必须去想象它是什么。

sentences.en: And you can take possession of something you imagine much more fully than something you just see reproduced in front of you.
sentences.zh: 比起那些仅仅呈现在你面前复制品，你可以更完整地占有你所想象的事物。

sentences.en: It's why I think we're nearly always disappointed when we see a film of a book.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我认为我们看根据书改编的电影时几乎总是会感到失望。

sentences.en: Because in reading the book, we've imagined the character of the place, and they've become ours, part of the way we live and think.
sentences.zh: 因为在阅读这本书时，我们已经想象了那个地方的角色，它们变成了我们的东西，成为我们生活和思考方式的一部分。

sentences.en: And the same with objects.
sentences.zh: 物品也是如此。

sentences.en: If you have to do the mental, imaginative work of creating the object for yourself, you are invested in it, you possess it in a way that is not really possible, I think,
sentences.zh: 如果你必须通过脑海中的想象来为自己构建这个物品，你就会投入其中，以一种我认为不可能的方式去拥有它，

sentences.en: with just an image.
sentences.zh: 仅仅通过一张图片。

sentences.en: I find that if you lead with the story of an object, you fall in love with it in a different way.
sentences.zh: 我发现，如果你以一个物品的故事切入，你会以一种完全不同的方式爱上它。

sentences.en: Whereas your visual reaction to maybe seeing Rosetta Stone is like,
sentences.zh: 而你对看到罗塞塔石碑的直观反应可能是，

sentences.en: I was expecting something more impressive or something like this.
sentences.zh: 我原本期待更震撼的东西或者类似这样的东西。

sentences.en: But you can tell the sort of the import of it, what it meant, all the story of how it was created, and, you know, even the mundane way which it existed.
sentences.zh: 但你可以看出它的重要性、它的含义、它被创造的整个故事，以及，你知道的，它存在时那种平淡无奇的方式。

sentences.en: I think that's right, because what we were really trying to tell was a hundred biographies of an object.
sentences.zh: 我认为这很对，因为我们真正想要讲述的是一个物体的百种传记。

sentences.en: I mean, because we only have one life, but objects have many, many lives.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，因为我们只有一生，但物体拥有非常非常多的生命。

sentences.en: And what we got very interested in was the changing role of the object through time.
sentences.zh: 而我们非常感兴趣的是，物体随时间推移而改变的角色。

sentences.en: In ways I mean, nobody, when the people carve the Rosetta Stone, this is a tax decree, it's a bit of a tax law.
sentences.zh: 某种程度上，当人们雕刻罗塞塔石碑时，这是一项税收法令，它有点像税法。

sentences.en: And it's so boring, beyond boring.
sentences.zh: 而且它是如此无趣，无趣透顶。

sentences.en: Nobody carving that tax law in the three languages for administrative purposes had any idea what it would one day come to mean.
sentences.zh: 为了行政目的用三种语言雕刻那项税法的人，绝对不会想到它有朝一日会变成什么样。

sentences.en: And there is something wonderful about that in an object, that the object can play a role that nobody could have guessed.
sentences.zh: 而物体身上有种奇妙之处，那就是物体能够扮演一个谁也猜不到的角色。

sentences.en: It makes their biographies much more engaging, much more alive, I think, than our own dull little predictable lives.
sentences.zh: 我认为这让它们的传记比我们自己沉闷、渺小、可预测的生活要吸引人得多，也生动得多。

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 完全赞同。

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 完全赞同。

sentences.en: So when you wrote and conceived of the series and produced it, you know, you were the head director of this august institution, the British Museum,
sentences.zh: 所以当你撰写、构思并制作这个系列节目时，你知道的，你是这个备受尊崇的机构大英博物馆的首席馆长，

sentences.en: as people hold it in great esteem.
sentences.zh: 正如人们对它抱有极高的敬意那样。

sentences.en: And I wondered if you noticed your relationship with the public changed when you weren't director, Neil McGregor.
sentences.zh: 我在想，尼尔·麦格雷戈，当你不再担任馆长时，你是否注意到你与公众的关系发生了变化？

sentences.en: You were my pal, Neil McGregor, who I'm inviting into my home to tell me a story about a cool thing.
sentences.zh: 你是我的朋友，尼尔·麦格雷戈，我邀请你到我的家里，给我讲一个关于酷炫物件的故事。

sentences.en: I think everybody's discovered that if you speak a lot on the radio, people feel they know you.
sentences.zh: 我想每个人都会发现，如果你经常在广播里讲话，人们就会觉得他们认识你。

sentences.en: And you must have said the same thing, that very disconcerting experience of actually being recognized in a lift by your voice.
sentences.zh: 你也一定有同感，那种在电梯里仅凭声音就被认出来的奇妙而又令人窘迫的经历。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: Is, the first time it happens, it's very, very peculiar.
sentences.zh: 这事儿第一次发生时，感觉非常、非常奇特。

sentences.en: And one of the things that I think is interesting about it is that it allowed us to reaffirm that the public collections in Britain, as in the United States,
sentences.zh: 我认为其中一件有趣的事情是，它让我们重申了英国的公共收藏，就像在美国一样，

sentences.en: are not the collections of the state, but the collections of the people.
sentences.zh: 不是国家的收藏，而是人民的收藏。

sentences.en: The people, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是人民的，对。

sentences.en: I mean, when the British Museum is created in the 1750s, the idea is that it should be the private collection of every citizen, not the collection of the king open to everybody.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当大英博物馆在18世纪50年代建立时，其理念是它应该成为每个公民的私人收藏，而不是向所有人开放的国王收藏。

sentences.en: Completely different conception from the continental European model.
sentences.zh: 这与欧洲大陆的模式有着完全不同的概念。

sentences.en: So, the idea of speaking directly into people's houses about their collection.
sentences.zh: 所以，这个想法就是直接走进人们的家中，谈论他们自己的收藏。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: Their things.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有的东西。

sentences.en: I mean, everything I was talking about belonged to the people listening to it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我所谈论的一切都属于正在收听的人。

sentences.en: Why did you choose to examine the 100 objects chronologically?
sentences.zh: 你为什么选择按时间顺序来研究这100件物品？

sentences.en: And what problems did that cause?
sentences.zh: 这带来了什么问题？

sentences.en: Or what solutions did it provide?
sentences.zh: 或者它提供了什么解决方案？

sentences.en: I think it has to be chronological, because one of the things that happens across human issues is that we create a technology, and then it helps us do something,
sentences.zh: 我认为它必须按时间顺序，因为人类发展中发生的事情之一，就是我们创造了一种技术，然后它帮助我们做某事，

sentences.en: and then we become completely dependent on it.
sentences.zh: 接着我们便完全依赖于它。

sentences.en: We can't live without it.
sentences.zh: 我们离不开它。

sentences.en: The hand axe, the simple stone-scraping hand axe, is what lets us, as humans, live anywhere in the world.
sentences.zh: 手斧，那种简单的刮削石斧，让我们作为人类能够在世界上任何地方生存。

sentences.en: But then, once you're there, you can't live without it.
sentences.zh: 但一旦你到了那里，你就离不开它了。

sentences.en: We've seen the same with mobile phones in the last 20 years.
sentences.zh: 在过去的20年里，我们在手机上也看到了同样的情况。

sentences.en: It opens something, and then it creates what can be a very dangerous dependency.
sentences.zh: 它开启了某些东西，然后又造成了一种可能非常危险的依赖关系。

sentences.en: So, that was one strand.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是其中一个主线。

sentences.en: And one of the key meta-narratives, I think, of any museum is the growing connectedness of the world.
sentences.zh: 我认为，任何博物馆的核心宏大叙事之一，就是世界日益紧密的互联性。

sentences.en: The fact that you can't tell a single story, to use Chimamanda Adichie's phrase.
sentences.zh: 用奇马曼达·阿迪希的话说，你无法只讲述单一的故事。

sentences.en: The story of the world is an interconnected story.
sentences.zh: 世界的历史是一个相互交织的故事。

sentences.en: So, if you like, why we wanted to do it chronologically was to show that constantly intensifying power of exchange, curiosity about other places, trade, greed, war, whatever.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果我们愿意的话，我们之所以想按时间顺序来做，是为了展示那种不断加剧的交流力量、对其他地方的好奇心、贸易、贪婪、战争，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But that has intensified steadily across the millennia, until you can't really tell a single narrative of a national story.
sentences.zh: 但这种力量在几千年来稳步加剧，直到你再也无法真正讲述单一的国家故事。

sentences.en: And that was one of the points we wanted to make.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们想要表达的观点之一。

sentences.en: The idea of a national history.
sentences.zh: 国家历史的概念。

sentences.en: I'm sorry to say that somebody was writing history in the United States.
sentences.zh: 我很抱歉地说，曾经有人在美国编写历史。

sentences.en: But the idea of a national history is unthinkable without situating that nation in the global context.
sentences.zh: 但如果不把国家置于全球语境中，国家历史的概念是不可想象的。

sentences.en: We are in agreement, for sure.
sentences.zh: 我们完全赞同。

sentences.en: But it does present this problem as, like, the beginning set of objects are all objects that are pre-historical.
sentences.zh: 但它确实呈现了这样一个问题：就像最开始的一组展品全都是史前物品一样。

sentences.en: There's not written records about them.
sentences.zh: 没有关于它们的文字记载。

sentences.en: Like, you have to sort of conceive of the story differently, because there isn't a record of how it was made or why it was made.
sentences.zh: 因此，你必须以不同的方式去构思这个故事，因为没有关于它是如何制作的或为什么制作的记录。

sentences.en: And so, your set of stories really gets sort of limited, and then it opens up as you go along.
sentences.zh: 所以，你的故事集在某种程度上确实受到了限制，然后随着你的深入而逐渐展开。

sentences.en: So, what was that like?
sentences.zh: 那么，那段经历是怎样的？

sentences.en: I disagree.
sentences.zh: 我不同意。

sentences.en: I disagree.
sentences.zh: 我不同意。

sentences.en: It narrows down the more we know about the...
sentences.zh: 我们了解得越多，范围就越小……

sentences.en: I guess that's true.
sentences.zh: 我想也是。

sentences.en: I mean, the whole point of, it seems to be, the central point of any kind of historical investigation is your poetic involvement with somebody else.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，任何历史研究的核心意义，似乎都在于你对另一个人的诗意参与。

sentences.en: That you have to think, what is it like to be somebody else?
sentences.zh: 也就是你必须思考，成为别人是什么感觉？

sentences.en: Because that's the basis of all tolerance.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一切宽容的基础。

sentences.en: I mean, if you like, the whole venture was really Gulliver's Travels.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话，整个探究其实就是《格列佛游记》。

sentences.en: You go off around the world, you find these astonishing things, wild things.
sentences.zh: 你周游世界，发现了这些令人惊叹的事物、狂野的事物。

sentences.en: But the point of Gulliver's Travels is not that the people in Brobding, Niagara, huge, and Lilliput, tiny.
sentences.zh: 但《格列佛游记》的重点不在于布罗卜丁奈格人巨大、利 Lilliput 人渺小。

sentences.en: The point is that when you come back to England, you realize we're pretty peculiar.
sentences.zh: 重点是当你回到英国时，你会发现我们其实很奇特。

sentences.en: We're the odd ones.
sentences.zh: 我们才是怪人。

sentences.en: And to denormalize, to remove yourself as the norm, is the precondition of tolerance.
sentences.zh: 去非常态化，不再将自己视作常态，是宽容的前提。

sentences.en: And that's what Gulliver's about.
sentences.zh: 这就是格列佛的故事。

sentences.en: It's what the British Museum's about.
sentences.zh: 这也是大英博物馆的意义所在。

sentences.en: And it's what the series was meant to be about.
sentences.zh: 这也是这个系列节目原本想要表达的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: That's interesting.
sentences.zh: 真有趣。

sentences.en: I love that approach.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢这种方法。

sentences.en: One of the things that I marveled at in the series is you're touching everything.
sentences.zh: 在这个系列中让我赞叹的一点是，你触及了方方面面。

sentences.en: You're always describing it as a first-hand experience.
sentences.zh: 你总是把它描述为一种第一手的体验。

sentences.en: And for one reason you do that, it's a little more radiophonic.
sentences.zh: 你这么做的一个原因，是它更有广播感。

sentences.en: It allows you to have something happening as you're talking, so it's not just a lecture.
sentences.zh: 它能让你在说话的同时发生一些事情，所以不只是单纯的讲座。

sentences.en: But the other part of it is it puts you in the first-person narrative of this object.
sentences.zh: 但另一部分在于，它让你进入了这个物体的第一人称叙事中。

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: The difficult thing about that, which I found very hard to know how to manage,
sentences.zh: 其中困难的部分，我也觉得很难掌握，

sentences.en: is where the object has, for the people who made it, and possibly for people today as well,
sentences.zh: 就是当这个物体对于制造它的人，以及可能对于今天的人们来说，

sentences.en: its own kind of sacred existence, its own life.
sentences.zh: 具有它自己那种神圣的存在、它自己的生命。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And how one ought then, with proper reverence, proper respect, hold or touch this object without having those beliefs.
sentences.zh: 那么在没有这些信仰的情况下，我们应该如何以适当的崇敬和尊重来持有或触摸这个物体呢？

sentences.en: And that took us into very interesting areas of the extent to which you study, can study,
sentences.zh: 这把我们带入了非常有趣的领域，即你在多大程度上可以研究、是否可以研究

sentences.en: objects in ways which are contrary to the belief patterns, belief assumptions of those who made them.
sentences.zh: 那些违背制造它们的那些人的信仰模式和信仰假设的物体。

sentences.en: How do we address an Australian original object, which may have sacred resonances in a respectful way?
sentences.zh: 我们如何以尊重的方式对待一件可能具有神圣共鸣的澳大利亚原住民物品？

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: So, one of the things I found, there's this moment in the series, quite late into it,
sentences.zh: 所以，我发现的一点是，节目中有一个时刻，在相当靠后的部分，

sentences.en: where you talk to David Hockney, which is the first person you talk to who made the object that you're talking about.
sentences.zh: 你与大卫·霍克尼交谈，这是你交谈过的第一个制作了你所讨论的物品的人。

sentences.en: Which is, it's such a change compared to the rest of the series.
sentences.zh: 这与该系列的其余部分相比真是个巨大的改变。

sentences.en: What was that like?
sentences.zh: 那是什么感觉？

sentences.en: Well, it was very thrilling.
sentences.zh: 嗯，非常激动人心。

sentences.en: We had been waiting to get to an object made by somebody where we could speak to the maker.
sentences.zh: 我们一直渴望能接触到由某个人制作的物体，这样我们就可以与创作者对话。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: The very first object, which was one and a half million years ago, one of the stone chopping tools.
sentences.zh: 最早的物品，是一百五十万年前的一件石制砍砸器。

sentences.en: Obviously, but we had David Attenborough instead.
sentences.zh: 显然，但我们请到了大卫·阿滕伯勒。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, that's pretty good.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那也相当不错。

sentences.en: Which is almost due to tell us what's going on, how this fits into the animal-human differentiation.
sentences.zh: 它几乎刚好告诉我们发生了什么，这如何融入动物与人类的区别中。

sentences.en: But it was wonderful with David Hockney because the objects we were talking about were a series of prints he'd made, really about gay life in Egypt.
sentences.zh: 但与大卫·霍克尼的交流非常奇妙，因为我们谈论的物品是他创作的一系列版画，主要关于埃及的同性恋生活。

sentences.en: And we chose the poems of Cavafy.
sentences.zh: 我们选择了卡瓦菲斯的诗歌。

sentences.en: And we chose the objects for several reasons.
sentences.zh: 我们出于几个原因选择了这些物品。

sentences.en: In the 20th century, we wanted to choose objects that would address the questions of new kinds of freedom.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪，我们希望选择能够探讨新型自由问题的物品。

sentences.en: So we had votes for women was one, gay rights another.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有女性投票权是一个，同性恋权利是另一个。

sentences.en: We wanted to, of course, to present what it was like to make the objects and why David himself, obviously very committed to gay rights,
sentences.zh: 我们当然希望展现制作物品的感受，以及大卫本人（显然非常致力于同性恋权利）

sentences.en: what it meant to him to read the poems above all.
sentences.zh: 阅读这些诗歌对他的意义是什么。

sentences.en: And then to make the prints, and then what it would mean to him to have the prints used, looked at, and spread the campaign, advance the campaign for gay rights internationally.
sentences.zh: 然后是制作版画，接着让这些版画被使用、被观看，并在国际上推动同性恋权利运动，对他的意义是什么。

sentences.en: So, but it was, as you say, it was a real turning point to be able to speak to the maker for the first time.
sentences.zh: 所以，正如你所说，能够第一次与创作者对话，真是一个真正的转折点。

sentences.en: There was also, there was a lot of excitement for the choice of the final 100th object.
sentences.zh: 还有，选择最后第一百个展品时引起了极大的兴奋。

sentences.en: You deliberately didn't reveal it until the last minute.
sentences.zh: 你故意保密到最后一分钟。

sentences.en: You invited listeners to suggest it.
sentences.zh: 你邀请听众提出建议。

sentences.en: What was it?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: Why did you choose it?
sentences.zh: 你为什么选择它？

sentences.en: And how did people react to it?
sentences.zh: 人们对此有何反应？

sentences.en: It was an enormous fun trying to decide what was the last object to choose.
sentences.zh: 决定选择最后一件物品的过程非常有乐趣。

sentences.en: We wanted to choose an object that spoke to a totally globalized world.
sentences.zh: 我们想选择一件能够代表一个完全全球化世界的物品。

sentences.en: We also wanted to end, of course, on a note that would be hopeful.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们还希望以充满希望的基调结束。

sentences.en: So, we eventually came down to two objects.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们最终锁定了两件物品。

sentences.en: One was a football shirt.
sentences.zh: 一件是足球衫。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: A football shirt of a West African, a footballer, a Drogba, a Francophone West African who was the great star of Chelsea.
sentences.zh: 一件西非足球运动员的球衣，德罗巴的球衣，他是切尔西的伟大球星，一位讲法语的西非人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And Chelsea was owned by a Russian oligarch.
sentences.zh: 而切尔西是由一位俄罗斯寡头拥有的。

sentences.en: Perfect.
sentences.zh: 完美。

sentences.en: And the football shirt had been made illegally in China, but bought in Latin America.
sentences.zh: 这件球衣在中国非法制造，却是在拉丁美洲买的。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So, that object seemed to us to pull together quite a lot of the world as it now is.
sentences.zh: 所以，在我们看来，这个物体似乎将当今的整个世界很好地串联了起来。

sentences.en: What we ultimately went for was slightly more serious.
sentences.zh: 我们最终选择的物品稍微严肃一些。

sentences.en: It was a solar panel rechargeable mobile phone.
sentences.zh: 那是一个太阳能充电的手机。

sentences.en: Because the mobile phone seemed to us to be the equivalent of the hand axe, the chopping tool.
sentences.zh: 因为在我们看来，手机就相当于手斧，也就是斩切工具。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: The first technology that had enabled humans to move around the world and this latest one that enabled humans to communicate around the world.
sentences.zh: 这是第一项让人类能够在全球范围内迁移的技术，而最新这项则让人类能够在全球范围内沟通。

sentences.en: We were interested in it because it's become, of course, in so many areas, an element of emancipation, particularly of women, enabling women to bank, enabling women to trade.
sentences.zh: 我们对它感兴趣是因为它自然而然地在许多领域成为了解放的象征，特别是对女性而言，让女性能够使用银行服务、进行贸易。

sentences.en: And, of course, the other dimension of solar power, which we wanted to bring in, is that in political terms, this has become a very important thing.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们想要引入的太阳能的另一个维度是，从政治角度来看，这已经变得非常重要。

sentences.en: Because in large areas of Africa and Asia, the electric currents, cables to areas, could be controlled by political bosses.
sentences.zh: 因为在非洲和亚洲的大片地区，电流和通往各地的电缆可能会受到政治首脑的控制。

sentences.en: And areas could either be not cabled or have cables removed or whatever.
sentences.zh: 这些地区可能无法通电、电缆被拆除，或者遭遇其他情况。

sentences.en: The solar power, at a stroke, removes that power, removes that political control.
sentences.zh: 而太阳能一举消除了这种权力，消除了这种政治控制。

sentences.en: So, it seemed to us to be in many, many ways an emblem of liberation, an emblem of the growing technologies which change our lives and then we become dependent on them.
sentences.zh: 因此，在许多方面，它似乎都成了获得解放的象征，成了改变我们生活并最终让我们对其产生依赖的新兴技术的象征。

sentences.en: It's also about talking.
sentences.zh: 它也关乎对话。

sentences.en: And, of course, many people listen to the BBC on their mobile phone.
sentences.zh: 当然，许多人都是通过手机收听BBC的。

sentences.en: So, it was also a nod to a patron.
sentences.zh: 所以，这也是对赞助商的一种致敬。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Radio is the most important thing.
sentences.zh: 广播是最重要的。

sentences.en: The BBC.
sentences.zh: BBC。

sentences.en: Of course, you know where your bread is buttered.
sentences.zh: 当然，你得知道谁才是你的衣食父母。

sentences.en: That makes sense.
sentences.zh: 这倒在理。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But it was also the solar-powered lamp, which also, like, extended the day.
sentences.zh: 但它也是太阳能灯，就像这样，延长了白昼。

sentences.en: And just, like, it's all about this sort of individualized freedom and the ability that this technology frees you for all kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 而且就像是，这一切都关乎这种个人化的自由，以及这项技术让你在各方面获得解放的能力。

sentences.en: That's what we wanted to, again, finish on how these technologies do, unquestionably, make life better.
sentences.zh: 这正是我们想要再次强调的结尾，即这些技术确实毫无疑问地让生活变得更好。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Because the solar panel will give you the lamp, which means you can work at home if you're a student, without interest, whatever.
sentences.zh: 因为太阳能电池板能为你提供电灯，这意味着如果你是个学生，你可以在家里学习，无需担心电网等问题。

sentences.en: And it also means you don't need to burn for your lighting materials which are likely to cause you lung problems and health difficulties.
sentences.zh: 这也意味着你不再需要燃烧照明材料，这些材料很可能会引起你的肺部问题和健康隐患。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, in every way, it's potentially a good thing.
sentences.zh: 所以，无论从哪个方面来看，这都可能是一件好事。

sentences.en: We wanted to end on a good hundredth thing.
sentences.zh: 我们想以一个美好的第一百个物件来收尾。

sentences.en: I'm interested in what you think of the series' legacy now.
sentences.zh: 我很想听听你对这个系列节目现在的遗产有什么看法。

sentences.en: It's an early example of podcasting being really successful.
sentences.zh: 这是播客取得巨大成功的一个早期例子。

sentences.en: I think it had more listeners globally than it did inside of the UK.
sentences.zh: 我认为它在全球的听众比在英国国内的还要多。

sentences.en: What do you think of the legacy of the show?
sentences.zh: 你如何看待这个节目的遗产？

sentences.en: Well, we've been as surprised by the legacy as we were by the response initially.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们对它的遗产感到的惊讶，和当初对各方反应的惊讶不相上下。

sentences.en: I think it has definitely had an impact in terms of reminding people that the everyday object has its own biography, its own history.
sentences.zh: 我认为它在提醒人们“日常物件也有其自身的传记和历史”方面，绝对产生了影响。

sentences.en: And that takes you back to the dignity of the maker and the user.
sentences.zh: 这会让你回想起制造者和使用者的尊严。

sentences.en: So, what it does as a history is it takes away the great moments that we're taught.
sentences.zh: 所以，作为一段历史，它的作用是抹去了那些我们被灌输的伟大时刻。

sentences.en: You don't have the Battle of Waterloo.
sentences.zh: 这里没有滑铁卢战役。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Why would it figure?
sentences.zh: 它怎么会出现在这里呢？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Because that's not the kind of history.
sentences.zh: 因为那不是那种类型的历史。

sentences.en: So, it opens the way to other histories told by other people.
sentences.zh: 因此，它为其他人讲述的其他历史开辟了道路。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And that's why a history versus the history.
sentences.zh: 这就是“一种历史”（A history）而不是“那段历史”（The history）。

sentences.en: A history.
sentences.zh: 一种历史。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that was very important.
sentences.zh: 这非常重要。

sentences.en: One of the slightly – it's been translated into a lot of languages, the book.
sentences.zh: 这本书被翻译成了很多语言，其中有一件稍微——让人头疼的事。

sentences.en: One of the vexing things is in some countries, some translations, the publisher insisted on making it the history.
sentences.zh: 令人烦恼的事情之一是，在某些国家的一些译本中，出版商坚持将其定名为“那段历史”。

sentences.en: So, that's maybe in translation, the and our mean different things in different languages.

sentences.en: The dynasty ended infamously with the reign of Cleopatra VII, the Cleopatra, who beguiled and seduced both Julius Caesar and Mark Antony.
sentences.zh: 该王朝以克利奥帕特拉七世的统治而声名狼藉，也就是那位迷倒并诱惑了尤利乌斯·凯撒和马克·安东尼的克利奥帕特拉。

sentences.en: But with the death of Antony and Cleopatra, Egypt was conquered by Augustus, whose image I'll be talking about later this week.
sentences.zh: 但随着安东尼和克利奥帕特拉的死，埃及被奥古斯都征服了，我将在本周晚些时候谈论他的形象。

sentences.en: And the Egypt of the Ptolemies became part of the Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 托勒密的埃及由此成为了罗马帝国的一部分。

sentences.en: In the next program, I'll be in Rome's great contemporary, China, looking at how the Han dynasty operated a super state and expanded their frontiers
sentences.zh: 在下一期节目中，我将前往罗马伟大的同时代国家——中国，看看汉朝是如何运作超级大国并拓展疆域的，

sentences.en: while keeping close control over every aspect of society.
sentences.zh: 同时对社会的方方面面进行严密控制。

sentences.en: Listen to the full 100 Objects series on Fridays, right here in the 99% Invisible feed.
sentences.zh: 每周五，欢迎在《99% Invisible》节目中收听完整的“100件文物”系列。

sentences.en: A History of the World in 100 Objects was a landmark collaboration between BBC Radio 4 and the British Museum.
sentences.zh: 《世界史：100件文物中的人类》是BBC第四电台与大英博物馆具有里程碑意义的合作项目。

sentences.en: If you'd like to hear more of A History of the World in 100 Objects, you can listen on BBC Sounds in the UK,
sentences.zh: 如果您想收听更多关于《世界史：100件文物中的人类》的内容，英国听众可以通过BBC Sounds收听，

sentences.en: and if you're outside the UK, you can find it wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 如果您身在英国境外，则可以在任何您获取播客的地方找到它。
